failure_modes.name: Query_Form_Mismatch
failure_modes.evidence: Hop 2 query: 'What evidence supports that Geoffrey Chaucer was the first poet buried in Poets' Corner at Westminster Abbey, and can you confirm the roles of John Feckenham as the last abbot and the formal name of Westminster Abbey as the Collegiate Church of St Peter at Westminster?' - This is a compound multi-part yes/no question bundling three separate verification targets rather than a focused retrieval query. Hop 3 query: 'Can you provide historical documentation or primary sources that confirm John Fecknam (also spelled Feckenham) served as the last abbot of Westminster Abbey, and specify when his tenure ended?' - Another natural-language question asking for documentation rather than a structured entity-focused query.

failure_modes.name: Query_Stagnation
failure_modes.evidence: Hop 1 retrieved passage [1] 'Geoffrey Chaucer...was the first poet to be buried in Poets' Corner of Westminster Abbey' and passage [2] 'John Feckenham...was an English churchman, the last abbot of Westminster.' Hop 2 query re-asked for confirmation of the same facts already provided: 'What evidence supports that Geoffrey Chaucer was the first poet buried in Poets' Corner...and can you confirm the roles of John Feckenham as the last abbot.' Hop 2 retrieval returned the identical Geoffrey Chaucer passage and identical Westminster Abbey passages as hop 1. Hop 3 query again sought John Feckenham information already retrieved in hop 1, and hop 3 returned the same John Feckenham passage a third time.

failure_modes.name: Verdict_Despite_Insufficiency
failure_modes.evidence: Summary 1 states: 'The claim is accurate. Westminster Abbey was formally titled the Collegiate Church of St Peter at Westminster. Geoffrey Chaucer was indeed the first poet to be buried in Poets' Corner at Westminster Abbey, as confirmed by historical records. John Feckenham (also spelled Fecknam) served as the last abbot of Westminster Abbey. All three assertions made in the claim are supported by the provided passages.' However, at the time of this summary (after hop 1), passage [2] about John Feckenham was present but the solver rendered a definitive 'accurate' verdict for all claims without noting any need for further verification, yet subsequent summaries acknowledge uncertainty about John Fecknam verification.

failure_modes.name: Solver_Irrelevant_Passage_Overprocessing
failure_modes.evidence: Hop 3 retrieved multiple passages completely irrelevant to the Westminster Abbey claim: 'Abbot of Holyrood' (about Edinburgh), 'Ivo of Ramsey' (about St Ives), 'Sawley Abbey' (about Lancashire), 'Abbot of Cambuskenneth' (about Stirling), 'Historical document' (generic definition), 'Primary source' (generic definition), 'Gervase of Blois' (different Westminster abbot), and 'John Flete' (historian). These consumed 8 of 10 retrieval slots but none advanced the claim verification, representing significant resource diversion.
